This compound is identified as a target of multiple entities, including Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase and Beta-D-Glucopyranosyl-(Z)-3-Hexenol, which in turn are targets of the same compound. The evidence indicates that this compound may interact with the transporter protein through a series of molecular pathways, possibly involving the modulation of anion transport activity. The presence of multiple targets suggests a possible role in cellular processes related to anion transport, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be elucidated. The strength of the evidence is moderate, with some variation in scores across the paths, but the consistent presence of the compound as a target of multiple entities supports a plausible functional relationship.
